title: Decision queue — what must be answered, in order, before anything is implemented
ranking_rule: P0 blocks a decision outright; P1 needs an out-of-sample test; P2 needs a policy call on existing analysis; P3 is housekeeping. Lower priority rows cannot be resolved before their P0 parents.
the_one_line_answer: One input blocks almost everything: a timestamped price. Nine prior sessions built nine dashboards because the price was missing and a dashboard was the only thing left to build. Everything else on this list can be closed by arithmetic, by a policy decision, or by transcribing Game Books that already exist.

queue.question: What number was actually available, and when?
queue.have: Nothing. No official NFL page probed on 2026-11-14 publishes a spread, a total or a price (probes P5, P6, P12). The repository can state what a price WOULD have to be; it cannot state what one WAS.
queue.missing: A timestamped price series with a named venue, an opening number and a closing number.
queue.why_it_blocks: Every downstream claim is unpriceable. Hit rate, ROI, edge, closing-line value, the fair/market/difference columns, the price-snapshot store and the staking block all collapse to blank without it. This is the single blocking input in the project.
queue.next_action: Choose one price source and licence/track it. It does not need to be official NFL data — no such thing exists — but it must be a named, timestamped, reproducible feed (a licensed odds API or a manual capture of a specific operator screen at a specific minute). Record the operator and the capture time on every row, or the row is worthless.
queue.cost: One subscription or one disciplined manual capture routine per week.
queue.resolves: Unblocks DQ-02, DQ-03, DQ-04, DQ-05 and the entire staking half of the leaderboard.
queue.status: OPEN — cannot be closed with official NFL sources alone

queue.question: Does the model's number beat the closing number, or only beat a naive baseline?
queue.have: The model beats every naive baseline we can compute. S1 spread MAE 9.40 vs 10.16 for the league-mean baseline on 104 games; B03 recent form is the only arm that comes close at 9.40. Nothing beats a real market number because no real market number exists in the repository.
queue.missing: The closing numbers for the same 104 games.
queue.why_it_blocks: Beating a naive baseline is not evidence of an edge; it is evidence the baseline is naive. Only the closing number is a fair test.
queue.next_action: Once DQ-01 is answered, backfill closing numbers for the 104 walk-forward games and recompute mean absolute error against them. Expect the model to lose to the close; that result is the useful one.
queue.resolves: Determines whether the origination work is a research artefact or a candidate.

queue.question: How many graded bets are needed before any leaderboard rank means anything?
queue.have: Exact planning figures computed from the observed hit rates. S1's 95% interval is [0.5001, 0.6854] on 104 bets; its lower bound does not clear the 0.5238 break-even rate. To confirm the observed 59.62% against the 52.38% break-even rate at 80% power needs roughly 580 graded bets; against a coin flip it needs roughly 330. The repository holds 104 games and zero settled bets.
queue.missing: Graded bets. There are zero settled bets, because there are zero prices.
queue.why_it_blocks: The repository currently ranks strategies on 104 games. At that size a 2–3 point hit-rate difference is inside one standard deviation (about 4.9 points). Any leaderboard built on it is a ranking of noise.
queue.next_action: Publish, next to every rank, the number of graded bets and the sample required for that rank to be meaningful. Do not award a medal below the required n. The ledger already contains a demotion gate; this is the same idea applied to promotion.
queue.cost: Free — it is arithmetic on the existing register.
queue.resolves: Makes the leaderboard honest without needing any new data.
queue.status: OPEN — arithmetic available now, policy decision required

queue.question: Which family is being corrected, and who decided?
queue.have: Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted values for the 8 correlations this session recomputed, plus the existing 12-strategy family. Both sets of adjusted values are published side by side.
queue.missing: A pre-registered statement of family membership, fixed before results are seen.
queue.why_it_blocks: With 8 correlations and 12 strategies, the family size is a design choice that changes every adjusted p-value. A family defined after the fact can always be made to produce a survivor.
queue.next_action: Write the family into the strategy registry before the next evaluation window: which strategies count as one family, and whether parlay and prop products are in the same family as singles.
queue.cost: One paragraph, written before the games.
queue.status: OPEN — policy decision, no data needed

queue.question: Do the Week 11 originated lines beat the Week 11 results?
queue.have: 13 fair lines originated on 2026-11-14 from the verified W1–W10 log, with the break-even distance for each. Week 11 games are unplayed.
queue.missing: The Week 11 finals, and a price to compare them to.
queue.why_it_blocks: It is the first genuinely prospective test in the project. It cannot be run early, and running it late is not a substitute.
queue.next_action: After the Week 11 games, grade the 13 lines exactly as Week 9 was graded: spread MAE, total MAE, moneyline Brier, with n. Publish the numbers whatever they say, and do not re-originate the lines afterwards.
queue.cost: One round of retrieval and one grading script run.
queue.resolves: Adds 13 games to a 104-game evidence base. Honest, but small.

queue.question: Does a below-the-46 replacement actually predict a worse outcome?
queue.have: A working method, proven on two clubs: the Week 10 Game Book compared with the Week 5 Game Book for WAS and NYG. 3 single-identity slot changes, 1 explained by an official Out designation (Lucas Patrick, concussion), 2 unattributed, and 6 unexplained absences of Week 5 starters from the Week 10 game-day listing entirely.
queue.missing: The same extraction for all 32 clubs across several weeks, joined to results.
queue.why_it_blocks: Two clubs cannot show whether depth loss predicts anything. The hypothesis is plausible and untested.
queue.next_action: Transcribe the Game Book lineups for every completed game in the log, build a per-club per-week depth-change variable, and regress the margin residual on it. This is the highest-value NEW signal available without a price feed.
queue.cost: 16 games per week, roughly 60 transcribed lines each. Mechanical.
queue.resolves: Turns the operator's availability requirement from a register into a testable feature.
queue.status: OPEN — method proven, scale not done

queue.question: Can a player-prop model be tested at all with the data held?
queue.have: 240 official Next Gen Stats QB rows across weeks 1 and 3–9, and two prop strategies (S11, S12) both of which scored WORSE than the naive baseline: skill −0.17% and −0.57%.
queue.missing: A player-level closing line, and a player-game log covering every player, not just qualified quarterbacks.
queue.why_it_blocks: Without a line there is no over/under event to forecast, so a prop model has nothing to predict. The two prop strategies currently forecast raw yards, which is not a bettable object.
queue.next_action: Either obtain player-prop lines, or stop calling the prop work a betting product and label it a descriptive yardage model. The current labels overclaim.
queue.cost: Free (relabelling) or one data licence (real work).
queue.resolves: Removes the most misleading category in the strategy library.
queue.status: OPEN — both prop strategies are negative-skill and unpriceable

queue.question: Do parlays deserve a separate leaderboard at all?
queue.have: Cross-game parlay S9 shows +6.38% skill on 51 pairs and a 1.27% lower bound; same-game side+total S10 shows +0.89% skill and a 0.95% interval that includes zero. The economics: at an assumed -110 per leg a 2-leg parlay needs each leg to win at the same rate as a single, so the parlay adds variance without adding expected value.
queue.missing: Prices, and a reason to prefer the parlay to the singles it is built from.
queue.why_it_blocks: A parlay leaderboard rewards variance. With no price there is no way to say whether the parlay's extra legs are compensated.
queue.next_action: Keep parlays on the leaderboard only as a diagnostic of the singles feeding them, and state that explicitly. Do not award a separate medal.
queue.resolves: Stops the leaderboard from rewarding correlated variance.

queue.question: Which of the published correlations may be used, and for what?
queue.have: 8 of 9 recomputed. C1 and C2 agree exactly with the published values. C5–C8 are ILLEGITIMATE as published because n counts QB-games, not games. C3 and C4 duplicate C2. C9 was not recomputed. After Holm on this declared family, only C5 and C6 survive — and both are tautological (passing yards are part of the offence that scores the points).
queue.missing: Nothing. The analysis is complete; the decision is not.
queue.why_it_blocks: Suggestion registers keep proposing correlation-based combos. The register currently cannot tell legitimate from tautological.
queue.next_action: Render the legitimacy verdict on every correlation the site publishes, and remove C5/C6 from any combo-pricing argument.
queue.resolves: Prevents the most common false signal in prop markets.
queue.status: OPEN — analysis done, publication policy undecided

queue.question: How much of a leaderboard result is luck, stated as a number?
queue.have: Per-arm luck decomposition. Every arm's hit-rate interval, its exact one-sided p-value against a coin flip, and the number of bets needed to confirm its own observed edge. Six arms currently beat a coin flip at 5% before any family correction: B11, S1, S2, S6, S7, S8.
queue.missing: A family correction applied to that list (DQ-04) and out-of-sample confirmation.
queue.why_it_blocks: At a 5% threshold with 18 arms tested, roughly one false positive is expected by construction. Six is more than one, but not much more, and the family correction decides the rest.
queue.next_action: Apply DQ-04's declared family to the ladder and publish the surviving count, then wait for DQ-05.
queue.resolves: Answers 'remove luck from the equation' honestly: luck is measured, not removed.

queue.question: May a strategy ever be staked, and under what gate?
queue.have: A demotion gate exists in ledger/ (rules D1–D8, unit tested, inert because no strategy is live). Break-even at -110 is 52.381%. The best arm's interval lower bound is 50.006%.
queue.missing: An approved promotion threshold, and prices.
queue.why_it_blocks: Without a number, a strategy either stays on paper forever or is promoted on vibes. Both are bad.
queue.next_action: Approve a numeric promotion gate, for example: 400+ graded bets, hit-rate interval lower bound above 54%, positive ROI at the recorded price, and no single week contributing more than 25% of the profit.
queue.resolves: Makes the demotion gate meaningful by giving it a promotion counterpart.

queue.question: Which of the eleven published workspaces is the site?
queue.have: Root dashboard, requirements/, ledger/, origination/, decision/, decision-review/, desk/, strict/, hub/, integration/, audit/, docs/ mirror. Each has its own as-of date and its own numbers.
queue.why_it_blocks: A reader comparing two pages gets two answers and cannot tell which is current. That is worse than one incomplete answer.
queue.next_action: Declare root the canonical surface, and reduce every other workspace to a one-paragraph pointer with its as-of date. Do not delete them; the archives are the audit trail.
queue.resolves: Removes the largest usability defect in the repository.

queue.question: What happens to this repository between sessions?
queue.have: Weekly snapshots on 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-14. Both were captured by hand, after the data had already gone stale by one to two weeks.
queue.missing: A scheduled refresh that captures the official pages without a session.
queue.why_it_blocks: Every page carries an as-of date for exactly this reason. A model that is two weeks behind the schedule is not a decision tool.
queue.next_action: Extend the existing GitHub Actions workflow to fetch and diff the official scores, standings, schedule and injury pages weekly, and fail loudly on a diff. The workflow scaffolding already exists.
queue.resolves: Turns a snapshot project into a maintained one.
